coordinate_frame.origin: ground under the first video camera (approx.)

scale.method: assumed hand-held camera height 1.51 m, checked against crosswalk stripe period (~1.0 m, GB 5768.3)
scale.note: DA3 metric depth suggested +23 %, rejected (inconsistent with road markings)

coordinate_frame.gltf_note: web/GLB exports are Y-up (glTF convention): x_gltf = x, y_gltf = z, z_gltf = -y
coordinate_frame.web_axes: glTF Y-up: x_gltf=x, y_gltf=z, z_gltf=-y (source Z-up)

camera_intrinsics.solver: pycolmap 4.2 incremental SfM, 859/859 frames registered, 0.54 px mean reprojection error

lighting.method: sun direction triangulated from the saturated sun blob in 13 frames

notes: Scale is estimated (camera height + crosswalk), about +-5 %.
Species are visual inferences, not botanical identification.
Branching, leaves and bark are generated by code; positions, heights, crown envelopes and colours are measured from the video.
Unobserved areas (inner lawn, far road half, building backs, rotunda far side) are conservatively inferred and flagged per asset.
Web edition uses twig-card foliage (LOD); research edition (individual leaves, .blend sources) stays on the server.

params._doc: runtime, seeded instancing in the web viewer: cells of cell_m around the camera

grass.note: tufts are instanced at runtime (seeded, deterministic) over the lawn meshes; the research scene stores explicit instance buffers (scene.json: scatters)
